definitions.definition: The evidence-backed process by which Echo rebuilds a bounded self-model from accepted identity events.
definitions.invariant: The projected self hash is a pure function of the verified ledger.
definitions.name: Autognosis

definitions.definition: The bottom-up view of Echo subjects, relations, events, policies, adapters, and tests.
definitions.invariant: Every local identity claim resolves to a validated typed artifact.
definitions.name: Local

definitions.definition: The holistic view of Echo as a portable identity capsule with one governed root.
definitions.invariant: Every global claim is reproducible from the same accepted ledger head.
definitions.name: Global

definitions.definition: The typed topology connecting Echo subjects, roles, evidence, persona, and expression surfaces.
definitions.invariant: Every relation endpoint exists and every role is explicit.
definitions.name: Spatiality

definitions.definition: The ordered history of identity observations, proposals, decisions, and accepted transitions.
definitions.invariant: Accepted history is append-only and hash-linked.
definitions.name: Temporality

definitions.definition: The policy and evidence rules that constrain which proposed identity changes may be accepted.
definitions.invariant: No protected mutation is accepted without an authorized reviewer and applicable evidence.
definitions.name: Causality

definitions.definition: A schema-valid subject, relation, source, event, or evidence record.
definitions.invariant: Unknown kinds and schema versions are rejected.
definitions.name: Existence

definitions.definition: The enforced separation between immutable core, mutable persona, expression assets, and experimental cognition.
definitions.invariant: Persona and avatar observations cannot overwrite immutable core identity.
definitions.name: Distinction

definitions.definition: Multiple independent evidence sources retained without premature identity fusion.
definitions.invariant: Each source keeps a distinct digest, trust grade, and binding mode.
definitions.name: Disjunction

definitions.definition: A typed relation accepted only when endpoints, roles, evidence, and policy jointly validate.
definitions.invariant: Invalid endpoint or truth bounds fail before ledger append.
definitions.name: Conjunction

definitions.definition: A proposed identity event moving through validation, policy review, reducer preflight, and acceptance.
definitions.invariant: An unprojectable or stale-head transition never enters accepted history.
definitions.name: Transition

definitions.definition: A verified snapshot or capsule sealed by schema versions, state hash, and ledger head.
definitions.invariant: Tampering changes verification output and is rejected.
definitions.name: Modular Closure

definitions.definition: A deterministic KSM cycle that diagnoses evidence gaps and emits a rejectable next proposal.
definitions.invariant: Equal evidence inputs yield equal cycle identity and repair candidates.
definitions.name: Recursion

definitions.definition: Local spatial architecture of identity contracts and package boundaries.
definitions.invariant: The structure view resolves to versioned artifacts and testable evidence.
definitions.name: Structure

definitions.definition: Local temporal flow from proposal to accepted projection.
definitions.invariant: The process view resolves to versioned artifacts and testable evidence.
definitions.name: Process

definitions.definition: Local causal authorization, validation, and rejection rules.
definitions.invariant: The control view resolves to versioned artifacts and testable evidence.
definitions.name: Control

definitions.definition: Global identity topology exported as a typed hypergraph.
definitions.invariant: The space view resolves to versioned artifacts and testable evidence.
definitions.name: Space

definitions.definition: Global continuity from genesis through replay and portable checkpoints.
definitions.invariant: The time view resolves to versioned artifacts and testable evidence.
definitions.name: Time

definitions.definition: Global governance linking human stewardship, policy, evidence, and recovery.
definitions.invariant: The causality view resolves to versioned artifacts and testable evidence.
definitions.name: Causality
